text: In 1999, an engineer bought over twelve thousand cups of chocolate pudding... just for the BARCODES.
David Phillips spotted a Healthy Choice deal: mail in barcodes, get free airline miles.
Ten barcodes, five hundred miles. Mail them early, and the miles DOUBLED.
Then he found the cheapest barcode in the store: pudding. Twenty-five cents a cup.
He cleared out store after store... and had a manager order more cases.
The problem? Twelve thousand barcodes to peel off. By hand. Before the deadline.
His fix: the Salvation Army. Volunteers peeled the barcodes... and the pudding went to people in need.
He spent about three thousand dollars. Healthy Choice sent him over a MILLION miles.
The donation even got him a tax write-off. And Hollywood put his pudding plan into an Adam Sandler movie.
Every twenty-five-cent cup earned about a hundred miles.
He wasn't buying dessert. He was buying a MILLION miles... and he gave the pudding to charity.
